Package Comparison Helpers

Muhammad Yaseen

Source: vignettes/ppgt_comparisons.qmd

1 Abstract

The functions compare_all_designs() and compare_all_designs_honest() are package comparison helpers. They summarize matrices returned by package constructors and attach package-specific labels. Their outputs should not be read as direct literature results.

2 Comparing Package Constructors At A Common Size 

comparison <- compare_all_designs(n = 64, prevalence = 0.01, alpha = 0.20)

The comparison table reports structural summaries such as \(J\), \(N\), \(\lambda_{\max}\), and the ratio \(J/N\).

3 Reading The Metrics

For a design matrix \(\mathbf{M} \in \{0,1\}^{J \times N}\), the helpers summarize:

  • \(J\): number of pools
  • \(N\): number of individuals
  • \(J/N\): tests per individual in the design summary
  • \(\lambda_{\max} = \max_i |\mathcal{J}_i|\): maximum column weight

These summaries are intentionally structural. They compare the realized matrix dimensions, row/column weights, and package reporting labels for the generated design objects. They do not prove optimality, establish a universal ranking, or replace family-specific theoretical guarantees.

5 Interpreting The Labels

The package prints labels such as Configuration, Error_Correction, and the entries in summary. Those labels are package-specific reporting choices for these helpers. They are useful for package navigation, but they are not formal paper-backed guarantees.

6 References

  • Shental, N., Levy, S., Wuvshet, V., et al. (2020). Efficient high-throughput SARS-CoV-2 testing to detect asymptomatic carriers. Science Advances, 6(37), eabc5961.
  • Ghosh, S., Agarwal, R., Rehan, M. A., et al. (2021). Tapestry: A single-round smart pooling technique for COVID-19 testing. Nature Communications, 12, Article 2995.
  • Hong, F. S., Shah, N., Briggs, A., et al. (2022). HYPER group testing for SARS-CoV-2: A flexible, easy-to-implement, and highly efficient method. Nature Communications, 13, Article 3626.
